description: Testing the effect of behavioural interventions on agri-environment scheme option selection This project follows a series of Choice Architecture Tests (CATs) that have been commissioned by Defra's Farming Directorate Behavioural Science and Analytics team. These CATs have tested various interventions in a hypothetical agri-environment scheme application environment to understand their effect on option selection. Key findings include: • CAT 1 : tested the effect of defaults (pre-selected actions) on a hypothetical Sustainable Farming Incentive (SFI) application. Results showed a statistically significant increase in the environmental quality of the agreement generated through defaults compared to the current SFI application design. • CAT 2 : tested the effect of defaults and guided selection on a hypothetical Countryside Stewardship (CS) mid-tier application. Results for CAT 2 also showed defaults being effective. Compared to the current CS mid-tier design & some aspects of guided selection tested during the experiment, defaults led to more spatially targeted actions being chosen (the primary outcome of the experiment) by farmers, which might indicate higher quality environmental agreements. • CAT 3 : tested the effect of geospatial functionality (presenting guidance on spatial priorities visually) and offering a default totaliser (that shows the potential financial reward for choosing options) on a hypothetical SFI application. description: The A12 / A14 Copdock Interchange is the key Strategic Road Network (SRN) junction serving Ipswich. It connects the A14 with the A12 towards London and towards the East Coast. Locally, it provides access to the town's main Park & Ride site, out-of-town retail park and regional Sixth Form College. Congestion and safety concerns at A12 / A14 Copdock Interchange were identified in Route Strategy reports from March 2017 and April 2014, with the junction experiencing high collision clusters and severe queuing during peak periods. Initial Stage 0 work in 2018 recommended options for improvements and as a result, work commenced to develop a scheme under Road Investment Strategy 3 (RIS3) Pipeline Port Access scheme. A number of possible solutions were considered during PCF Stage 1 and two options were then taken forward into PCF Stage 2. A non statutory public consultation held in the autumn of 2021 and following the consultation, further assessments and consideration of alternatives was undertaken. A recommended option was selected, which was still subject to approvals, for a Preferred Route Announcement (PRA). description: Homes England is seeking a supplier to design and deliver an industry survey for Homes England and the National Housing Bank (NHB). title: S30180 Road Safety Strategy Support
description: This contract is to provide specialist analytical support to strengthen National Highways' approach to achieving its RIS3 road safety targets. Current forecasts indicate a material gap against the ambitious safety outcomes set for the road period, and there is a need for a robust, evidence-based understanding of which interventions will have the greatest impact on reducing casualties and delivering value for money. This commission will bring together and assess the 34 measures contained within the Government's Road Safety Strategy, National Highways' Road to Zero Harm plan, the RIS3 safety programme, and wider stakeholder insight. The objective is to develop a prioritised programme of road safety interventions supported by clear evidence of effectiveness, costs and benefits, including metrics such as cost per KSI prevented. The outputs will provide a critical evidence base for both the delivery of National Highways' own safety programme and engagement with key stakeholders, including DfT, ORR, the Road Safety Strategy Implementation Board and Ministerial Boards. The work will identify gaps in current interventions, assess additional opportunities, evaluate feasibility and effectiveness, and produce a prioritised roadmap of actions and recommendations to support improved safety outcomes across the wider road network.

To support this ambition, ONR intends to commission a comprehensive cultural climate assessment. This requirement aligns with ONR's 2030 Strategy and responds to expectations set out in the UK Government Review of Nuclear Regulation. It is intended to reinforce ONR's cultural foundations and ensure that organisational behaviours, leadership practices and working environments are aligned to strategic objectives. ONR recognises that organisational culture is dynamic and continually evolving. Senior leadership plays a critical role in shaping culture through decision making, behaviours and the environment created across the organisation. As such, cultural improvement must address both: • Structural factors (e.g. governance, organisational design); and • Infrastructure factors (e.g. leadership behaviours, decision making norms, psychological environment). title: Activity & Interpretation Plan Consultant
cpv_description: Research and development services and related consultancy services
description: The appointed consultant will prepare a comprehensive Activity & Interpretation Plan which demonstrates how people will engage with St Peter's Church and the wider heritage of Thetford through: • Learning; • Volunteering; • Skills development; • Community engagement; • Interpretation; • Participation; • Events; • Training; • Outreach activities. The consultant shall ensure that the Activity & Interpretation Plan is fully aligned with NLHF requirements and capable of supporting a successful Delivery Phase application. The Activity Plan shall identify opportunities for community involvement, volunteering, learning, training, events and wider public engagement, together with recommendations for sustainable delivery and long-term legacy. The Interpretation Plan shall identify and communicate the key heritage themes, stories and significance of St Peter's Church, establish target audiences, and develop recommendations for accessible and engaging interpretation that supports the project's vision and outcomes. The Consultant shall ensure that both plans are fully integrated and aligned with the requirements of the National Lottery Heritage Fund and other funding stakeholders, providing a practical framework for implementation during the Delivery Phase. description: To deliver a community-led Arts, Crafts and Heritage Capacity Building Programme in the Slieve Gullion DEA, working with community groups from the Forkhill and Newtownhamilton areas. The programme should use arts, crafts, cultural heritage and creative skills development as a vehicle for building organisational capacity, increasing skills and confidence, supporting knowledge exchange, and creating opportunities for participants to learn from one another through practical activities, shared experiences and networking opportunities. The programme should celebrate and explore the rich cultural and heritage assets of the area while creating opportunities for participants from different backgrounds to connect, collaborate and develop lasting relationships. buyer: Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs
description: Designing and Testing Behaviourally-informed Interventions (Understanding and Addressing Vaccine Uptake and Hesitancy Across Livestock Disease Programmes) The overall aim of this project is to develop an evidence-based understanding of the behavioural and social factors that influence vaccine uptake and hesitancy across a range of animal disease contexts, and to identify opportunities to improve the effectiveness of vaccination as a disease prevention, control and preparedness measure. The project will generate evidence to support the design and implementation of future vaccination policies and programmes, ensuring that behavioural considerations are integrated alongside epidemiological, economic and operational evidence. Specifically, the project seeks to: • Improve understanding of the factors influencing livestock keeper, veterinary and wider stakeholder decisions relating to vaccination. • Identify common and disease-specific drivers, barriers and motivations affecting vaccine uptake, hesitancy and participation in vaccination programmes. • Explore if and how behavioural influences vary across disease contexts, stakeholder groups, sectors and policy settings. • Understand the role of trusted advisers, social networks, markets, supply chains, industry bodies and institutions in shaping vaccination decisions. • Assess behavioural challenges associated with routine preventive vaccination, disease eradication programmes, and emergency vaccination deployed during disease outb…

title: SCC APC Digital Post-mortem Facility - Bagshot (CT Scanner Suite)
description: This procurement seeks to secure a digital post-mortem service in Surrey utilising Computed Tomography (CT) scanning technology. This will support the local authority in meeting its statutory responsibilities under the Coroners and Justice Act 2009 while helping to manage increasing pathology costs and improve service delivery. By providing a non-invasive alternative to traditional post-mortem examinations, CT scanning will significantly reduce the number of invasive procedures undertaken, helping to preserve the dignity of the deceased and improving the experience of bereaved families, particularly those from faith communities with specific cultural or religious requirements. It will also present opportunities for future income generation and operational efficiencies, supporting the long-term sustainability of the Coroner's Service. In doing so, it contributes to the Council's strategic priority of ensuring that no one is left behind by delivering a more compassionate, accessible, and inclusive service for Surrey residents.

description: The tender opportunity (Tender 65/2026) will be published on Simply Do platform under the challenge titled: Predicting Demand. Managing Tomorrows Visitors, Today. "How can local authorities anticipate and manage visitor demand and movement across key destinations, while understanding the factors driving these changes, so they can proactively mitigate potential impacts before they become a problem." This challenge is focused on transforming how local authorities manage visitor destinations. Using Castlewellan Forest Park as a real-world test environment, the initiative addresses the growing pressures that large rural tourism destinations face from fluctuating visitor demand, which impacts local roads, parking, waste services, biodiversity, and infrastructure. Historically, council management has relied on static measures and reactive interventions, such as annual visitor numbers or seasonal passes, which fail to provide real-time insights or predictive intelligence. The proposed project aims to transition local authority management from a fragmented, reactive approach to a connected, evidence-led, and predictive decision-making model.

description: The Tring Grounds Project delivers a comprehensive enhancement of the museum's external landscape, creating a more accessible, engaging and environmentally diverse visitor experience. The proposals include a reconfigured arrival and parking area, improved pedestrian circulation routes, new accessible pathways through the grounds and woodland, and strengthened connections between key visitor destinations. A geology trail forms a central interpretive element of the scheme, incorporating chalk and stone specimens sourced from local and regional geological contexts to help visitors engage with the area's geological history. Hard landscaping works include new paths, seating, interpretation features, gathering spaces and carefully detailed surface treatments designed to improve accessibility and visitor comfort. Soft landscaping proposals introduce a new orchard, meadow and woodland enhancements, habitat creation, strategic planting and ecological management measures that support biodiversity while enriching the character of the site. Together, the landscape, geology and interpretation elements create a coherent visitor journey that celebrates the museum's scientific mission, encourages outdoor learning and exploration, and improves the functionality, accessibility and sustainability of the grounds.

description: The University of Plymouth invites expressions of interest from suitably qualified and experienced organisations for the supply, installation, commissioning and support of a Time-of-Flight Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometer (TOF-ICP-MS) to support frontier environmental and analytical research. The University requires a Time-of-Flight Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometer (TOF-ICP-MS) with both single particle and single cell analytical capabilities. The system must achieve limits of detection at parts-per-billion (ppb) concentrations and particle size detection capabilities of approximately 15 nm. The instrument must be capable of simultaneous multi-element and isotopic analysis, enabling the quantification of multiple elements and their isotopes within individual particle or cell events in complex environmental matrices. The equipment will support laboratory-based fundamental and frontier research programmes. The proposed solution must include all ancillary equipment necessary for operation, including a suitable autosampler, desolvation system and specialist software for instrument control, data acquisition and data analysis. The software should support the quantification and reporting of particle mass, particle size and number concentration data. title: London's Violence Reduction Unit - Pan London Tertiary Service
buyer: Mayor's Office For Policing And Crime
description: About the VRU The London Violence Reduction Unit (VRU), hosted within the Mayor's Office for Policing and Crime (MOPAC), pioneers a partnership-based public health approach to tackling violence rooted in prevention and early intervention. Since 2019, the VRU has invested in over 550,000 targeted interventions for young people across London. Project Background The VRU takes a public health approach to violence reduction, recognising that prevention requires action at different stages. Primary prevention seeks to change the conditions that make violence more likely, strengthening protective factors before violence occurs. Secondary prevention responds when risk or violence is emerging, aiming to interrupt risk and prevent escalation. Tertiary prevention focuses on reducing the harm caused by violence, supporting recovery and reducing the likelihood of further violence. title: SMRU Seal Flipper Feasibility Study
description: Project Aims The aim of this commission is to undertake a strategic feasibility study assessing the suitability of existing seal telemetry and electronic flipper-tag technologies for supporting future seal monitoring, assessment, and reporting requirements within the UK. The study will review current evidence, technologies, deployment approaches and animal welfare considerations, identify evidence gaps and technical limitations, and evaluate opportunities for future telemetry development. The commission will provide an evidence-based roadmap to support future investment decisions relating to seal telemetry research and technology development. 3. Project Background The Special Committee on Seals (SCOS) has identified robust estimation of UK seal population size and demographic processes as a high research priority. Current monitoring and assessment approaches rely on telemetry-based estimates of haul-out behaviour to support population estimation, particularly for harbour seals. However, existing telemetry evidence remains limited, and uncertainties persist regarding variation in haul-out behaviour, movement ecology, survival, connectivity and demographic parameters. At the same time, significant technological developments have occurred in wildlife telemetry and biologging systems. Interactives will embody the gallery’s key principles: - Playful – inspires and celebrates active exploration, curiosity, fun and experimentation. - Social – appeals to both children and their accompanying adults, sparks intergenerational conversations and encourages sharing discoveries and ideas with others. - Inclusive – is multi-sensory, values diversity, strives to be ‘Open for All’ and is accessible to as many people as possible. - Inviting – welcoming, with a sprinkling of Manchester personality, intuitive to navigate and empowering independent exploration. title: Coding NDNS Consumption data into EFSA’s food classification+description -FoodEx
suppliers: Creme Software Ltd (trading as Creme Global)
description: As part of the FSA’s commitment to ensure food is safe and is what it says it is, the FSA undertakes food safety risk assessments which underpin these decisions in line with the internationally recognised ‘Codex Working Principles for Risk Analysis for Food Safety’. A key component of food safety risk assessment is exposure assessment, which estimates the amount of a hazard consumed through the diet. Exposure assessment combines food consumption data with information on the concentrations of substances such as contaminants, food additives or pesticide residues in food to estimate the levels consumers may be exposed to. To conduct UK dietary exposure assessments, the FSA uses consumption data in combination with occurrence data for hazards and other substances in food. UK consumption data is primarily obtained from the UK National Diet and Nutrition Survey (NDNS). The National Diet and Nutrition Survey (NDNS) is a co-funded programme between the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) Office for Health Improvement and Disparities (OHID) and FSA. NDNS is a rolling programme which assesses the diet, nutrient intake and nutritional status of the general population of the UK. Tenders are invited to carry out the recoding of NDNS consumption data to FoodEx2, a standardised system for classifying and describing food.

title: ES RDE 183 - Legacy Soil Phosphorus Mobilisation Review
description: Environment Agency Self-Service Direct Award. Phosphorus (P) is an essential nutrient for crop growth and food production, with agricultural inputs primarily supplied through inorganic fertilisers and organic manures. However, manures are often applied to meet crop nitrogen (N) requirements, which can result in excess P applications and the gradual accumulation of legacy P in soils. This increases the risk of P losses through runoff, erosion, and leaching, contributing to eutrophication of watercourses. As P is frequently the limiting nutrient in freshwater ecosystems, even small releases can cause detrimental environmental impacts, including algal blooms and oxygen depletion. In England, around 55% of rivers and 75% of lakes fail to meet phosphorus standards under the Water Framework Directive.

title: Support in the Community
description: Lot 3 Shared Lives This service involves providing person centred support to individuals from one or more of the following primary adult user groups: • Learning Disabilities • Physical Disabilities • Autism • Sensory Impairment • Brain Injury / Neurological Condition • Older People and older people with Dementia • Mental Health • Dual Diagnosis (any of the above) Shared Lives is a longstanding form of care that centres on sharing home, family and community life, in supporting people to lead fulfilling and active lives. Shared Lives schemes are an alternative to home care, supported living and residential care for people in need of care and support. Shared Lives is used by around 15,000 people in the UK. In Shared Lives schemes, a Shared Lives Carer and someone who needs support get to know each other and, if they both feel that they will be able to form a long-term bond, they share homes, family and community life. This can mean that the person becomes a regular daytime or overnight visitor to the Shared Lives Carers household, or it means that the person moves in with the Shared Lives Carer. Shared Lives schemes provide individuals with the opportunity to stay in the homes of individually recruited, trained and approved Shared Lives Carers and their families who live in the community. description: Blackburn with Darwen Borough Council is looking to procure a Direct/Indirect Community Reparation and Unpaid Work Service. Children and Young People (CYP) who offend and made subject to an out of court or court disposal are systematically assessed, helped and directed to change their behaviour and encouraged to make amends to the victims of their crimes. One of the ways in which CYP can make amends is to carry out reparation either directly to the victim or, when this is not possible or practical, to the community as a whole. The aim of the Service is to offer CYP an opportunity to participate in restorative activity following the commission of an offence directly to their victim or to the wider community. The primary objectives of the Service will be to: • Enable young people to make amends to victims and/or their community. • Promote and model pro-social behaviours to support young people to avoid reoffending and integrate into the community. • Ensure that young people do not pose a risk to the public or themselves whilst participating in reparation/unpaid work sessions. • Enable young people to access effective programmes linking in with learning outcomes to improve their education, training and employment opportunities. ...

description: The purpose of this specification is to commission the provision of vapes and associated products to help people in Sheffield to quit smoking as part of the city’s tobacco dependency treatment services. This is in replacement of the national swap to stop programme which ended in April 2026. Nicotine vapes are recommended as a first choice stop smoking aid as there is strong evidence that they work, doubling the chances of a successful quit attempt. While vaping is not risk-free, the latest review of evidence concludes that vaping, in the short and medium term, is significantly less harmful than smoking cigarettes and poses a small fraction of the risks of smoking. E-cigarettes are not recommended for non-smokers and should certainly not be used and cannot legally be sold to people who are younger than 18 years old. The successful provider will provide access to vape starter kits (e-cigarettes and associated products) via a voucher scheme to individuals who choose to adopt this method of quitting. title: COBR Strategic Partnership (Private Sector Resilience Project)
description: The purpose of this Prior Information Notice (PIN) is to notify all interested parties of the Cabinet Office's intention to undertake a commercial procurement exercise. The exercise aims to appoint a world-class Strategic Partner to provide a managed service. The Cabinet Office Briefing Rooms (COBR) Directorate requires a world-class strategic partner to co-design and co-deliver high-impact, targeted resilience workshops, scenario exercises, and potential follow-on consultancy to UK and international private sector clients. The primary objective is to operationalise resilience within the private sector by translating central government crisis doctrine and leadership expertise into actionable strategies for C-suite executives and operational leads, aligned with existing industry practice. COBR serves as the central hub for the UK Government's whole-of-government crisis response mechanism. National resilience is a whole-of-society endeavour. This partnership seeks to support business and organisational resilience by establishing a scalable framework for clients to adopt UK-standard crisis doctrine while creating a formal feedback loop where private sector insights directly inform future national resilience policies. This agreement is a zero-cost contract to the public buyer. The Cabinet Office will not pay the partner.
